question.text: A balloon was moving upwards with a uniform velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. An object of finite mass is dropped from the balloon when it was at a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the ground level. The height of the balloon from the ground when object strikes the ground was around: (takes the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Object is projected as shown so as per motion under gravity, 

S=ut+12at2

-75=+10t+12(-10)t2⇒t=5 s

Object takes t=5 s to fall on ground height of balloon from ground, 

H=75+ut

=75+10×5=125 m
